edges.description: A constitutively open calcium-permeable channel in the keratinocyte plasma membrane admits unregulated calcium influx.
Calcium overload through the constitutively open channel is cytotoxic to the cells expressing it.
TRPV3 forms a signalling complex with TGF-alpha/EGFR in keratinocytes, and TRPV3 channel activity stimulates TGF-alpha release, so constitutive channel activity transactivates EGFR.
Keratinocyte TRPV3 couples to protease-activated receptor 2 signalling and to nerve growth factor release, through which hyperactive channel activity is transmitted to pruriceptive sensory neurons.
Elevated keratinocyte apoptosis was proposed to drive compensatory epidermal turnover and hyperkeratosis.
EGFR signalling drives keratinocyte proliferation; its inhibition with erlotinib resolves the keratoderma, which is the strongest evidence that this signalling sustains the hyperkeratosis.
Excess TGF-alpha/EGFR activity produces hairless phenotypes in mice, and TRPV3 controls hair morphogenesis through this complex.
Palmoplantar hyperkeratosis is the direct clinical expression of the epidermal process.
The same hyperkeratotic process around the mouth, nose, eyes, anus and genitalia.
Nail abnormalities accompany the keratoderma; the nail unit is a keratinizing epithelium.
Circumferential hyperkeratosis around digits forms constricting bands.
Thick, fissuring plantar and palmar keratoderma is painful and limits walking and grasping.
Hyperkeratosis over the digits and joints restricts joint movement.
Leukokeratosis of the oral mucosa is a keratinizing lesion of the same disordered epithelium.
Fissured, hyperkeratotic skin is the site of the recurrent bacterial and candidal infections.
Defective hair growth from constitutively active follicular TRPV3 presents as alopecia.
Acute inflammatory flares of the extremities with vasodilatation, redness and burning pain present as erythromelalgia.

evidence.reference_title: Abnormal Somatosensory Behaviors Associated With a Gain-of-Function Mutation in TRPV3 Channels.
evidence.snippet: We re-derived the Trpv3G573S mutants using 129S1/SvlmJ eggs; the animals obtained were then backcrossed to 129S1/SvlmJ background for six-eight generations.

nodes.description: Loss-of-function model, the inverse of the human lesion: Trpv3-null mice have wavy hair and curly whiskers, the phenotype of TGF-alpha and EGFR loss-of-function mutants, and defective skin-barrier cornification. It establishes the TRPV3-TGF-alpha/EGFR axis that the gain-of-function variants overdrive.

evidence.reference_title: TRP channel regulates EGFR signaling in hair morphogenesis and skin barrier formation.
evidence.snippet: Unexpectedly, we found that mice lacking the Trpv3 gene also exhibit wavy hair coat and curly whiskers.

nodes.description: A third substitution of the Gly573 hotspot, found in a patient whose immunological work-up showed hyper-IgE, eosinophilia and frequent skin infections.

evidence.reference_title: Olmsted syndrome: exploration of the immunological phenotype.
evidence.snippet: The patient was found to harbour a previously undescribed 1718G-C transversion in TRPV3, causing a G573A point mutation.

nodes.description: The first and most recurrent Olmsted syndrome variant, identified de novo in the index trio and in three further patients; the same substitution occurs spontaneously in the hairless DS-Nh mouse.

evidence.reference_title: Exome sequencing reveals mutations in TRPV3 as a cause of Olmsted syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Using whole-exome sequencing of case-parents trios, we have identified a de novo missense mutation in TRPV3 that produces p.Gly573Ser in an individual with OS.

nodes.description: A heterozygous variant in exon 15 found in a patient with classic Olmsted syndrome and in his father, treated with erlotinib. The source abstract calls c.1964T>C a frameshift mutation, but a single-nucleotide substitution producing p.Leu655Pro is a missense change, as the article title states; the same residue was reported as L655P in the genotype-phenotype series.

evidence.reference_title: Erlotinib therapy for Olmsted syndrome with p.L655P missense mutation in the TRPV3 gene: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Notably, a previously unreported heterozygous frameshift mutation, c.1964 T > C (p.L655P), was identified in exon 15 of the TRPV3 gene in this patient and his father.

nodes.description: A recurrent S4-S5 linker variant associated with severe disease and erythromelalgia-like inflammatory flares.

evidence.reference_title: A new TRPV3 missense mutation in a patient with Olmsted syndrome and erythromelalgia.
evidence.snippet: Whole exome sequencing of patient DNA identified a novel de novo heterozygous missense mutation within TRPV3, p.Leu673Phe, predicted to be damaging.

nodes.description: A familial variant segregating through three generations with a mild, partly nonpenetrant, atypical phenotype (sclerodactyly-like fingers in the proband, focal plantar plaques in the grandfather); it increases apoptosis of HaCaT keratinocytes but less than the classic hotspot variants.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation in TRPV3 gene causes atypical familial Olmsted syndrome.
evidence.snippet: However, TRPV3 sequencing results revealed an identical heterozygous mutation c.2016G > A in the proband, his mother and his maternal grandfather

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation in TRPV3 gene causes atypical familial Olmsted syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, a functional assay indicated that the Met672Ile mutation imposed a more significant induction of apoptosis on HaCaT cells compared with that of the wild type.

nodes.description: Substitutions of Trp692 in the TRP domain, each identified as a de novo heterozygous variant in a patient with the classic mutilating phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Olmsted syndrome in an Iranian boy with a new de novo mutation in TRPV3.
evidence.snippet: TRPV3 was sequenced and a new de novo heterozygous missense mutation, c.2076G>C (p.Trp692Cys), was identified.

nodes.description: An atypical variant in exon 8 reported in an adult with mutilating keratoderma who developed plantar squamous cell carcinoma.

evidence.reference_title: Case report: Novel p.Val306Met missense mutation in TRPV3 in a case of Olmsted syndrome accompanied by squamous cell carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: Genetic analysis identified a novel heterozygous p.Val306Met missense mutation in the exon 8 of TRPV3.
